name: Task_10
description:
Estimate aluminum's constant-volume heat capacity. Run one continuous temperature cycle with targets 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 K, then directly 300 K. Preserve positions and momenta at every stage boundary, including the return to 300 K.

Build periodic 108-atom aluminum by repeating a conventional cubic FCC cell with lattice parameter 4.05 Å by 3 x 3 x 3. Use the supplied MACE-MP-0 ASE calculator without dispersion and keep the cell fixed. Initialize Maxwell-Boltzmann momenta once at 300 K with a recorded seed and remove center-of-mass momentum once. Preserve the cell, positions, and momenta throughout the cycle and retain a calculation log with your own code.

Use Langevin, NVTBerendsen, NoseHooverChainNVT, Bussi, or Andersen for fixed-cell NVT. Choose numerical settings and extend sampling until each stage is settled. Use a timestep 1 fs, at least 2 ps equilibration and 3 ps production per stage, and at least 32 production samples spaced at most 100 fs apart. When resuming, preserve the model, seed, cumulative time, cell, positions, and momenta.

Production averages use all samples strictly after equilibration. Derive kinetic energy as sum(p^2/m)/2 in ASE units, total energy as potential plus kinetic energy, and temperature with 3N degrees of freedom.

Fit mean total energy per atom against mean measured temperature for exactly the five forward stages (indices 0–4, targets 300–700 K). Use ordinary least squares with an intercept by default; optionally declare results.fit with method="wls" and five positive weights, or method="theil_sen" (median pair slope and median y-slope*x intercept). Return only results.heat_capacity (slope in eV/(atom K)). The evaluator derives kB_per_atom by dividing the slope by ASE units.kB.

Retain production samples from all seven forward plateaus, 300 through 900 K. Each plateau mean measured temperature must be within 10% of its prescribed target; the heat-capacity fit still uses only the first five forward plateaus.
